audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings tell the reader to defend against Irelia with Null Sphere's shield - wants.you[1] 'use Null Sphere's shield to absorb her stacked-passive trades', early 'Hold Q to shield her burst', spikes[2] 'your Q shield eat her stacked-passive trades', whys[4] 'your Q shield soak her stacked-passive trades'. Null Sphere's shield absorbs MAGIC damage and Irelia is physical damage end to end. The page even contradicts itself inside one sentence in late: "Your passive's 15% magic reduction is wasted against her physical damage, but your raw mobility and Q shield aren't" - the Q shield is magic-only for exactly the same reason the passive is.
audit.why: The reader is being told, four times, to bank a cooldown as armour that will absorb none of the incoming damage, and the one place the page notices the problem it exempts the wrong tool. What the page should have said instead is the mirror image, and it is genuinely decisive: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage while she charges it, and every point of Kassadin's damage is magic - so her main defensive cooldown pays nothing against you and you can burst straight through the charge. Second omission: Flawless Duet sends out two blades that converge, and only enemies caught BETWEEN them are stunned. Seven separate strings say 'dodge her E' and not one says how.
audit.corrected: The magic shield re-tasked from armour to what it actually does here (absorbing your own trade-back window and last-hitting); Defiant Dance's physical-only reduction added as the burst window; the between-the-blades stun condition written in.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q: shield 'absorbs magic damage'; P: 'takes reduced magic damage')
champ-data/_kits/irelia.json (W Defiant Dance: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge'; E Flawless Duet: 'Enemies caught in between are damaged, stunned and Marked')

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet is named the clock the lane runs on in seven places without a cooldown; Vanguard's Edge, her ultimate, is never named at all; and the whys array is shifted by one slot at Levels 4-5 and Level 6, so the Level 6 explanation ('Riftwalk arrives') is printed against Levels 4-5, where Kassadin does not have Riftwalk.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s - the longest thing in her kit and a real window once spent. Bladesurge is 10/9/8/7/6s but refreshes outright on a Marked target or a kill, so its printed cooldown almost never applies in a wave. Vanguard's Edge is 125/105/85s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s. And a reader at level 4 following whys[3] would step up expecting a blink they will not have for two more levels.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet's 16s and Bladesurge's reset condition added; Vanguard's Edge named with its 125s; whys[3] rewritten for the actual Levels 4-5 stage and whys[4] for Level 6, closing the off-by-one.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Irelia six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while spikes[3] ends 'This is your kill window', late says 'the game tips your way', and whys[6] says she 'can't pin a Kassadin who never stops moving'.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 52% over 25 games. The front-loading to Irelia is right, but a chart with no Kassadin stage cannot produce a winning record, and it contradicts its own text at the last stage.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Kassadin in both layers. Everything earlier left as it was.

audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia on every dash, and she dashes constantly because the cooldown refreshes off Marked targets and kills. In a lane where she resets through the wave to reach you, that heal is continuous rather than occasional, which is what makes Grievous Wounds a lane purchase rather than a teamfight one.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named against Bladesurge's heal in the all-in block.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json (Q: 'Irelia dashes forward to strike her target, healing herself')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late tells you to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. tldr, winCon and report[9] all call Irelia 'he' and 'his'.
audit.why: Riot's Null Sphere text is damage, channel interrupt, and a magic-absorbing shield. The pronouns are boilerplate leaking from other matchups onto a female champion.

edits.before: Irelia owns this stretch and you have to accept it. She Bladesurge-dashes onto your caster minions to reset the cooldown and close on you, stacking her passive for free while your Null Sphere is single-target poke that empties your mana bar for one chunk. Don't try to win a trade. Last-hit at max range, and if she E-stuns you just walk rather than feeding a full stun-into-Bladesurge combo. Hold Q to shield her burst, not to chip her.
edits.after: Irelia owns this stretch and you have to accept it. She Bladesurge-dashes onto your casters to refresh the cooldown and close, stacking her passive free while your Null Sphere is poke that empties your mana. Flawless Duet stuns only what is caught BETWEEN the two blades, so step off the line they converge on rather than backing straight up. Spend the Q on minions: its shield absorbs magic, and she deals none.

edits.before: Level 6 is when you stop being free food. Riftwalk finally lets you blink out of her Bladesurge dash-chain, reposition out of her E stun, and escape the jungle ganks she sets up. Land Nether Blade on her or a minion to refund mana so you can keep farming under tower, and keep Null Sphere up to shield her poke. Once your Catalyst into Rod of Ages comes online the lane sits even, so don't force a fight, just deny her the snowball and let the game go long.
edits.after: Level 6 is when you stop being free food. Riftwalk finally lets you blink out of her Bladesurge dash-chain, step off the line between her two Flawless Duet blades, and escape the ganks she sets up - her E is 16s at rank 1, so a whiffed one is a real window. Land Nether Blade on her or a minion to refund mana so you can keep farming under tower. Once Catalyst into Rod of Ages comes online the lane sits even, so don't force a fight; deny her the snowball and let the game go long.

notes: FOUR strings told the reader to defend against Irelia with Null Sphere's shield ('absorb her stacked-passive trades', 'Hold Q to shield her burst', and two more). That shield absorbs MAGIC damage; Irelia is physical end to end. The page even contradicted itself inside a single sentence in content.late - "Your passive's 15% magic reduction is wasted against her physical damage, but your raw mobility and Q shield aren't" - when the Q shield fails for precisely the same reason the passive does. Re-tasked to raw HP from Rod of Ages, which is what actually soaks her. THE INTERACTION THAT WAS MISSING is the exact mirror of that and it favours Kassadin: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage while she charges it, and every point Kassadin deals is magic, so her main defensive cooldown pays nothing against him and he can burst through the charge. Also added: Flawless Duet stuns only what is caught BETWEEN its two converging blades - seven strings said 'dodge her E' and none said how; Bladesurge refreshes outright on a Marked target or a kill, so its printed 10s almost never applies in a wave; and Vanguard's Edge, her ultimate, was never named in either layer. Fixed: breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence; tldr, winCon and report[9] called Irelia 'he'/'his'. ARRAY MISALIGNMENT: whys[3] (Levels 4-5) described Riftwalk arriving, which happens at Level 6, and whys[4] (Level 6) described the first-item stall - a one-slot shift that would have a reader at level 4 stepping up expecting a blink they do not have. Both rewritten to their correct stages. LEVEL CHART: no stage read Kassadin on a 52% win rate; 2+ items flipped. NOT WRITTEN: _missing-interactions lists 'Irelia can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Flawless Duet (E)'. That derives from a 'channel' flag on Kassadin's Q, but Riot's text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels - it is not itself one. I left the claim out.
